A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Consistency Deep Equilibrium Models by the same authors. All main-text and appendix material is readable, and retained equations, experiments, figures, and tables can be matched across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original C-DEQ evaluations on WikiText-103, ImageNet, ogbn-arxiv, and ogbn-products, together with convergence, ablation, and memory results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark evaluations and adds solver comparisons, architectural and hyperparameter ablations, and measurements of distillation and caching costs.

M1.justification: Algorithm 4 replaces Gaussian-random initialization with z0 = 0, resolving its inconsistency with the zero initialization already specified in v1 Section 3.1. The AA-based student, consistency losses, time mappings, and inference procedure otherwise remain unchanged. This establishes a correction to the documented procedure, without establishing an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four datasets for language modeling, image classification, and graph node classification. The added experiments vary solvers, architectures, and hyperparameters within existing coverage; the ImageNet split revision belongs to evaluation protocol.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 are retained. V2 adds targeted comparisons against Picard and Broyden teacher-trajectory solvers and MLP/GRU replacements for the student AA module (Tables 4 and 9). The separate comparative memory experiment is removed; its NDEQ comparator cites the same work called HyperDEQ elsewhere.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands evaluation design through controlled solver substitutions, architecture/history/schedule sweeps, and measurements of cached-trajectory and distillation costs, while removing the memory-versus-NFE experiment. Existing setting descriptions also change: Appendix A.2 specifies ImageNet validation evaluation instead of the 150,000-image test-set description, and Table 6 specifies SGD for ImageNet C-DEQ instead of v1's blanket Adam statement. These are reported protocol revisions, without evidence establishing reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained convergence plots, AA-removal experiment, and loss-coefficient grid, v2 tests teacher-solver choice, AA versus generic history-processing modules, history-window size, gamma/rho/beta sensitivity, and alternative time mappings (Tables 4 and 9–13). Appendix A.4 replaces the comparative memory-scaling analysis with distillation and trajectory-caching overhead analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results continue to use point estimates.

E6.justification: The main accuracy/perplexity entries are retained, while Tables 1–3 fill previously missing explicit-baseline runtimes. Numerous results are added, including WikiText-103 perplexities of 26.43/26.97/28.68 for AA/Broyden/Picard (Table 4) and 2.6 hours of distillation versus 36.2 hours of teacher pretraining (Table 7). V1 Table 5's comparative memory results, including C-DEQ's 3.2–3.4 GB series, disappear; v2's peak distillation-memory measurements concern different conditions.

T1.justification: Equation (2) changes from the explicit residual flow dz/dt = f_theta(z,x) - z to a conceptual solver-induced field G_theta(z,t). Section 3.1 introduces history-dependent AA dynamics and conditions equilibrium correspondence on well-posedness. This is a substantive but bounded mathematical reformulation; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims about few-step consistency distillation, the AA structural prior, combined local/global losses, 2–20× accuracy improvements, and up to 20× faster inference. The solver-induced terminology refines the framing without introducing a different central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges teacher-pretraining costs, dependence on trajectory stability, and the limited theoretical scope of the FP-ODE perspective. It adds interpretations concerning AA-specific inductive bias, history-versus-latency tradeoffs, and modest offline overhead, while dropping the comparative memory-advantage discussion. Appendix C.5 largely elaborates the teacher well-posedness explanation already present in v1 Section 4.2.

D1.justification: V2 adds per-dataset optimizer, learning-rate, weight-decay, and dropout configurations (Table 6), concrete schedule and augmentation defaults, cached-trajectory sizes, and training-cost details. It newly documents teacher-weight initialization and baseline evaluation without small-NFE retuning. A repository URL replaces the supplement-only code pointer; its availability is not verified by the local PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chen, Jiang, and Vuik (2025) to support the solver-induced interpretation of AA. It also attributes augmentation settings to CLLM and teacher initialization practice to HyperDEQ/Skip-DEQ. The main related-work positioning is retained; updates to existing Kipf and Kou references are bibliographic.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely intact, with localized rewrites in Sections 3.1 and 4.3, grammar corrections, and updated author/publication and acknowledgement text. V2 adds an experiments appendix, moves the existing Discussion appendix from B to C, and expands the conclusion heading to include limitations.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the tabular presentation with solver, configuration, cost, and ablation tables (Tables 4 and 6–13), and removes v1's memory table. Retained tables and Figure 3 are repositioned, while the loss grid moves from Table 4 to Table 5. Figures 1–3 retain their substantive visual content, with minor label corrections.

improvement.justification: The added controlled ablations, implementation settings, and offline-cost measurements make the design and efficiency claims easier to assess; the initialization correction and explicit limitations also improve clarity. These benefits are moderated by removal of the comparative memory evidence, conflicting AlexNet parameter counts in Tables 2 and 6, and broad robustness wording despite substantial sensitivity in Table 11. The revision provides a useful but limited net quality improvement.
